statements.label: ex:following_example_skeletal_itemize
statements.scope_notes: WP-24a, audited clean (wave 1, WP-24). Partial: tagged sorry: dimension theory: a closed totally disconnected subset of R^n is zero-dimensional and a subset of dimension <= n-2 does not separate R^n (Hurewicz-Wallman Thm IV 4 / Alexander duality / Borsuk separation). Not in mathlib; mathlib's countable-complement argument does not reach uncountable K, and straight-line general position fails (a Cantor set can meet every ray from a point). Everything else of item 4 (chart localisation, transfer of total disconnectedness through univBall, density) is proved.; local structure theory of geometric simplicial complexes, absent from mathlib (carrier of a point, open stars as a neighbourhood basis of K.space, star of a point as the cone on its link, connectedness of an open simplex with its open codimension-one faces, and the general-position step that a path avoiding the (n-2)-skeleton crosses facets only through open (n-1)-faces). The reduction k < n-2 to k = n-2 is proved (GX.isSkeletal_skeletonSpace). Readings taken: 'surface' read as a Hausdorff space charted on R^2 (no second countability, no smoothness). | 'tame knot' read as a closed locally flat subset (charts onto open subsets of R x R^2 sending the knot to R x {0}); the circle structure is unused. | 'Cantor wildly embedded' read as a closed totally disconnected subset (compactness and perfectness unused). | 'pure n-dimensional simplicial complex' read as a finite geometric complex (mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex) in a finite-dimensional real normed space with the subspace topology; pure = every face has <= n+1 vertices and lies in a face with n+1 vertices.
statements.notes: WP-24a, audited clean (wave 1, WP-24). Partial: tagged sorry: dimension theory: a closed totally disconnected subset of R^n is zero-dimensional and a subset of dimension <= n-2 does not separate R^n (Hurewicz-Wallman Thm IV 4 / Alexander duality / Borsuk separation). Not in mathlib; mathlib's countable-complement argument does not reach uncountable K, and straight-line general position fails (a Cantor set can meet every ray from a point). Everything else of item 4 (chart localisation, transfer of total disconnectedness through univBall, density) is proved.; local structure theory of geometric simplicial complexes, absent from mathlib (carrier of a point, open stars as a neighbourhood basis of K.space, star of a point as the cone on its link, connectedness of an open simplex with its open codimension-one faces, and the general-position step that a path avoiding the (n-2)-skeleton crosses facets only through open (n-1)-faces). The reduction k < n-2 to k = n-2 is proved (GX.isSkeletal_skeletonSpace). Readings taken: 'surface' read as a Hausdorff space charted on R^2 (no second countability, no smoothness). | 'tame knot' read as a closed locally flat subset (charts onto open subsets of R x R^2 sending the knot to R x {0}); the circle structure is unused. | 'Cantor wildly embedded' read as a closed totally disconnected subset (compactness and perfectness unused). | 'pure n-dimensional simplicial complex' read as a finite geometric complex (mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex) in a finite-dimensional real normed space with the subspace topology; pure = every face has <= n+1 vertices and lies in a face with n+1 vertices.
paper_findings: Item 3 (l.372) is false as written: the bow-tie (two closed triangles of R^2 sharing only the vertex 0) is a finite pure 2-dimensional simplicial complex whose 0-skeleton is not skeletal: a small open star of 0 is connected, removing 0 disconnects it (GX.bowtie_counterexample, built as a mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex). The item needs local strong connectivity in codimension >= 2 (every two n-simplices containing a simplex of dimension <= n-2 are joined through (n-1)-faces containing it), as for normal pseudomanifolds; the bow-tie fails exactly this (GX.not_isLocallyStronglyConnected_bowtie). The same caveat applies to l.625 ('gluings of projective polyhedra ... complement of the (n-2)-skeleton ... skeletal'), which is true for gluings that are pseudomanifolds but not for arbitrary face gluings.

Item 4 (l.373) needs n >= 2: in R no nonempty subset is skeletal (GX.eq_empty_of_isSkeletal_real), so a Cantor set in a 1-manifold is not skeletal. 'Wildly' presupposes n >= 3 anyway, so this is a precision rather than an error; the statement holds for tame and wild embeddings alike.

The closure properties l.383-390 never use Hausdorff; the two map items (l.389, l.390) need only the SOURCE locally connected; 'U portly in X, U ⊆ V implies U portly in V' (l.385) holds for an arbitrary subset V, not only open ones, when X is locally connected.

statements.label: prop:GX_sing_morph_local
statements.scope_notes: WP-24e, audited clean (wave 1, WP-24). Partial: a reading awaiting the author Readings taken: The paper does not define the a.e. structure induced on an open (or portly) subset W, nor 'locally an a.e. morphism'. Read: 'f|W is an a.e. morphism' = some U ⊆ W, portly in W (Portly's subtype convention), on which f induces a (G,X)-morphism into Reg N (IsAEMorphismOn); 'locally' = every point has an open W with f|W an a.e. morphism. Under this reading all three equivalences are proved.

paper_findings: Read literally, a set with empty preimage is evenly covered (vacuously), so every point outside the closure of p(X) is ordinary (GX.compl_closure_range_subset_ordY). This is what makes the two claims 'ord(Y) = ∅' at l.872 and l.880 false.

paper_findings: l.844: with mathlib's notion of covering map (fibres may be empty, total space need not be connected), ord(X) → ord(Y) is a covering whenever X is locally connected, connected or not (GX.isCoveringMap_restrict_ordX). If 'covering' includes surjectivity, connectedness of ord(X) is NOT the only obstruction: for the spread Unit → Bool, () ↦ true, ord(X) = Unit is connected and ord(Y) = Bool, but the restriction misses false (GX.unitTrue_counterexample), again because of the vacuous evenly-covered sets. It does hold for a surjective p (GX.surjective_restrict_ordX).

statements.label: cex:portlyness
statements.title: Portlyness of X_1
statements.scope_notes: WP-24d, audited clean (wave 1, WP-24). Partial: paper statement corrected (DEC-27) Readings taken: l.877: 'the coarsest topology making the natural injection X → Y a spread' — such a coarsest topology is not obviously well defined (spreadness depends on components, which depend on the topology). Which topology is meant: the one generated by the subspace-topology components of X ∩ U?
statements.notes: WP-24d, audited clean (wave 1, WP-24). Partial: paper statement corrected (DEC-27) Readings taken: l.877: 'the coarsest topology making the natural injection X → Y a spread' — such a coarsest topology is not obviously well defined (spreadness depends on components, which depend on the topology). Which topology is meant: the one generated by the subspace-topology components of X ∩ U?
paper_findings: Item 1 holds and is proved as a theorem (GX.notMem_ordX_of_notMem_interior).

Item 2, l.880: 'ord(Y) = ∅' is false as written: p(X) avoids the open unit disc (‖p(x)‖ ≥ 1), so the disc is (vacuously) ordinary whatever topology X carries (GX.ball_subset_ordY_portlyInv). The intended claim is ord(Y) ∩ p(X) = ∅.

Item 2's own space (X ⊆ ℝ² with 'the coarsest topology making the injection a spread') is not built. A counterexample with every property the paper lists (X = ℝ connected, Hausdorff, second countable, locally path-connected; p = x ↦ ||x|-1| a spread; X₁ = (1,∞) open and locally connected in X but not dense; Y₁ = (0,∞) open; X₁ → Y₁ a homeomorphism) is GX.cex_portlyness: 1 ∉ ord(Y), 2 ∈ X₁ ∖ ord(X), and p^{-1}(Y₁) ∋ -2 so p^{-1}(Y₁) ≠ X₁.
